evidence: src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:120-161. I compared each fields tuple with the MySQL 8.0/8.4 documented INFORMATION_SCHEMA column lists and ordinal order. I did not run SHOW COLUMNS against a live server. TABLES has 21 columns, from TABLE_CATALOG through TABLE_COMMENT, in documented order. COLUMNS has 22 columns, from TABLE_CATALOG through SRS_ID, in documented order, including GENERATION_EXPRESSION and SRS_ID. KEY_COLUMN_USAGE has 12 columns, from CONSTRAINT_CATALOG through REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME, in documented order. __post_init__ also requires fields to be distinct and kept to be a subset of fields. No omitted or misordered column found.

rule_sets.py:128 keeps 4 TABLES fields, :140-144 keeps 12 COLUMNS fields, :154-158 keeps 9 KEY_COLUMN_USAGE fields, which makes 25 (matches criterion 5). _CatalogView.__post_init__ (:113) requires kept to be a subset of fields. _catalog_body (:403-421) projects the quoted field when it is in spec.kept, and `NULL AS <field>` for every other field in spec.fields. Field counts are 21/22/12, matching the test at test_safety_rule_sets.py:392-400 and the NULL-count assertions at :376 and :387. No kept field leaks outside the rule set: _catalog_filter (:363-400) restricts rows to the current schema and listed tables or columns. For key rows it also requires the referenced schema, table and column to be listed or NULL. The wrapping derived table carries LIMIT, so the model's conditions cannot reach hidden rows. The kept values (names, types, keys) describe only the listed tables and columns.

Installed sqlglot 30.31.0 (within >=30.22,<31). generators/mysql.py:842-843 currentschema_sql returns self.func('SCHEMA'), so exp.CurrentSchema() emits SCHEMA(), which MySQL documents as a synonym of DATABASE(); the MySQL parser maps both SCHEMA and DATABASE to exp.CurrentSchema (parsers/mysql.py:151-152). For the cast, generators/mysql.py:709-717 cast_sql only remaps types in CAST_MAPPING (321+), which has no BINARY entry (BINARY is not in CHAR/SIGNED mappings), so the DataType renders as BINARY, giving CAST(x AS BINARY). MySQL accepts that and compares byte for byte in WHERE. rule_sets.py:341-350 builds exactly these nodes. I read the source and did not run the generator.

rule_sets.py:166 sets _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT to 18446744073709551615, the maximum unsigned 64-bit value that MySQL documents as the largest LIMIT value. _catalog_body (lines 416-421) applies it with .limit(exp.Literal.number(...)) as a plain numeric literal, so the MySQL dialect emits LIMIT 18446744073709551615. MySQL documents that a LIMIT in a derived table prevents merging into the outer query, which forces materialization. Pushing outer conditions into a materialized derived table is a separate optimization, which I did not check against MySQL docs or the optimizer. The connector test tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:627-638 sends WHERE IF(TABLE_NAME='rs_salaries', EXP(1000), 0) > 0. Unguarded, that raises an OperationalError. Through the rule-set chain it returns 0 rows. I did not run the test; I read it and relied on MySQL's documented behavior.

rule_sets.py:269-271 _analyze is annotated to return tuple[list[exp.Table], list[tuple[exp.Table,str]]] (base, catalog), and it is built from two separate lists. Its only caller, apply_rule_set (576-587), unpacks `base, catalog = _analyze(tree, tables)` and calls `_rewrite(tree, base, catalog, tables)`, which matches the 4-arg signature at 424-429. It calls `_rewalk(tree, tables, expected)` twice, matching 515-519. In the tests, every `guard._rewalk(tree, TABLES)` call (test_safety_rule_sets.py:265-522) uses the 2-arg form, which is valid because `expected` is optional. The monkeypatch test at 594-607 replaces _analyze and _rewrite with *args/**kwargs stubs. No direct test calls to _analyze or guard._rewrite exist. The method RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite (614) is a separate method that takes only sql. I did not read the unpacking of the _analyze return past line 284.

rule_sets.py:448 and 481-483 use body.args.get("from_") is not from_, and requirements.txt:103 pins sqlglot==30.31.0. tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:440 also uses tree.args["from_"]. rule_sets.py:42 has `from __future__ import annotations`, so the `expected: _BodyTextCache` annotation at line 470 is not evaluated at import, although the class is defined later at line 496. `_rewalk` (line 515) uses `_BodyTextCache(tables)` at line 525 only at call time, after the module has fully loaded. The other use at line 578 is also inside a function. Type checkers resolve forward references at module level.

safety/rule_sets.py:507-509 text() raises ValueError when `tables is not self._tables`. The only call to text() is in _is_catalog_derived (:493), which is called only from _rewalk (:533) with the same `tables` and `expected` that _rewalk received. _rewalk is called only from apply_rule_set (:579, :587), where `expected = _BodyTextCache(tables)` (:578) is built from the same `tables` argument and passed to both re-walks. If expected is None, _rewalk builds the cache from its own `tables` (:525). RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite (:619-622) calls tables_for once, which returns a fresh dict per call (rule_sets.py:261), and passes that one object to apply_rule_set. So every path uses one identical object, and no copy or re-fetch occurs between the cache and its use. The ValueError would fail closed (:637-643) if that ever broke.

rule_sets.py:544/546 the re-walk raises RuleSetRefusal (subclass of UnsafeSqlError, line 184). RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (629-646) wraps _rewrite: RuleSetRefusal is re-raised (634-636); any other exception, including the ValueError raised at 373/387/509 by _catalog_filter/_BodyTextCache, is caught by `except Exception` (637-643), logged, and converted to RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNCHECKED). RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql (735-749) passes RuleSetRefusal through and redacts other UnsafeSqlError/RlsError. The tool layer query_database.py:727-734 turns UnsafeSqlError into a sanitized RuntimeError, and the generic handler at 739-744 covers the rest, so nothing escapes as an unguarded crash. Caveat: the exact MCP wire format beyond these handlers was not traced, but the guard-level and tool-level handling is structured.

rule_sets.py:120-147 keys are TABLES, COLUMNS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE; rls.py:185 set is {tables, columns, key_column_usage}. Qualification: rule_sets._catalog_view (247-258) requires db Identifier, no catalog, db.lower()=='information_schema', name.upper() in keys. rls._is_rule_set_catalog_view (188-203) requires db Identifier, catalog None, db.lower()=='information_schema', name.lower() in set, plus dialect=='mysql'. The only extra check in _catalog_view (table.this is an Identifier) cannot matter, since a non-Identifier this has no name in the set. The extra mysql check is the dialect the guard targets. So every table the guard rewrites is skipped by RLS.

rule_sets.py _parse (lines 197-217): any statement that is not exp.Query (SHOW -> exp.Show/Command, DESCRIBE -> exp.Describe, TABLE shorthand) raises RuleSetRefusal(KIND_NOT_ONE_SELECT) at lines 206-209; unparseable ones are refused at 199-201. Other catalog lookups: _check_reference (231-239) refuses any db/catalog-qualified table, with KIND_CATALOG for information_schema/mysql/performance_schema/sys; only INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES/COLUMNS/KEY_COLUMN_USAGE are allowed via _catalog_view (247-258), and an unlisted view such as SCHEMATA falls to _check_reference and is refused. Hostile input considered: SHOW TABLES / DESCRIBE customers / SELECT from information_schema.SCHEMATA; all refused. NULL part: _CATALOG_VIEWS (120-161) projects every non-kept field as NULL (_catalog_body 406-411); TABLE_ROWS, DATA_LENGTH, TABLE_COMMENT, COLUMN_DEFAULT, COLUMN_COMMENT, CONSTRAINT_NAME are not in any kept set, so the prompt's statement that row counts, sizes, defaults, comments and constraint names read as NULL matches.

In src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py, _analyze (269-303) sends each source table through _catalog_view (247-258). That returns a view only when db is an Identifier equal (case-insensitive) to information_schema, there is no catalog part, and the upper-cased name is in _CATALOG_VIEWS (TABLES, COLUMNS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE). Every other reference goes to _check_reference (231-244). It refuses any db or catalog qualifier: KIND_CATALOG for information_schema, mysql, performance_schema and sys, KIND_QUALIFIED_TABLE for any other schema. It also refuses table-function sources and unlisted unqualified names. So traced inputs: information_schema.STATISTICS has no matching view, hits the db qualifier and is refused as a catalog read. mysql.user, performance_schema.x and sys.x are refused the same way. x.information_schema.tables has a catalog part, so _catalog_view returns None and it is refused. Mixed-case INFORMATION_SCHEMA is lower-cased and handled. An unqualified catalog-style name is refused as unlisted unless the rule set itself lists it, and that is the set's own table, not a catalog relation. References that scope analysis misses are caught by the tree.find_all(exp.Table) fallback (296-302), which calls _check_reference and then refuses. The re-walk (_rewalk, 515-546) also demands guard-built wrappers. I found no counterexample, so the docstring claim holds.

rls.py:188-203 _is_rule_set_catalog_view is true for dialect mysql, db Identifier information_schema (case-insensitive), no catalog, name in {tables,columns,key_column_usage}. Both match sites honor it: base-source loop (rls.py:300-303) continues before injection; final backstop (rls.py:331-336) sets own_name_skipped so match falls to alias only (alias match is not 'own name'). Without skip_catalog_views (default False) both checks are inert, so matching is unchanged. factory.py:129 sets skip_catalog_views=rule_sets is not None, only RlsGuardRunner caller (safety/__init__.py:199-204). Dialect from sqlglot_dialect_for_url returns 'mysql' for mysql URLs. Hostile input tried: catalog-qualified def.information_schema.tables is not skipped, but it is not one of the rewritten views and the rule-set guard refuses it (rule_sets.py:235-239, _catalog_view requires no catalog), so the claim's scope holds. Docs line 50 matches.

rule_sets.py:469-493 _is_catalog_derived returns True only if the table is a catalog view with args {this, db}, sits as the sole From of a Select that is the `this` of a Subquery wrapper (no extra args, no alias columns), and _generate(body) == expected.text(view, tables), where the expected text is _generate(_catalog_body(view, tables)) (496-512). _rewalk (515-544) raises RuleSetRefusal for any source table that is neither guard-derived nor catalog-derived. Any table not accounted for also raises. Trace of a catalog view outside a derived table, such as a plain FROM or a JOIN: table.parent is not a From whose parent is a wrapped Select, so it returns False and _rewalk refuses. Whitespace and quoting differences in the input are normalized by regeneration, so the claim's 'generates the same MySQL text' wording is accurate. Text comparison is on generated SQL, not node equality, which matches the claim. The re-walk runs on both the rewritten tree and the reparsed output.

rule_sets.py:120-161 lists the kept fields per view. _catalog_body (403-421) projects every non-kept field as NULL. _catalog_filter (363-400) requires TABLE_SCHEMA = current schema and a listed table. COLUMNS and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE also require a listed (table, column) pair. A key row survives only when it has no reference, or when its referenced schema, table and column are listed in the connected schema. _catalog_view (247-258) rewrites only information_schema TABLES, COLUMNS and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE. Any other reference goes through _check_reference (231-244), which refuses qualified names, including mysql, performance_schema and sys via _CATALOG_SCHEMAS (88). That includes information_schema.STATISTICS or VIEWS, which are qualified and not rewritten. SHOW statements fail the isinstance(tree, exp.Query) check in _parse (208-209). Absolute-claim input traced: information_schema.STATISTICS and performance_schema.x are refused, and a key row referencing an unlisted table is filtered out. Tests at tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:459-483 assert refusal for SHOW TABLES, SHOW COLUMNS, INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STATISTICS, INFORMATION_SCHEMA.VIEWS and mysql.user. performance_schema and sys are not tested, but they take the same _check_reference path as mysql.

skip_catalog_views defaults False in apply_rls (rls.py:212) and RlsGuardRunner.__init__ (safety/__init__.py:177). factory.py:129 sets it only as `rule_sets is not None` (rule_sets = cfg.rule_sets.loaded, line 110). The only RLS logic change in the diff is the skip gate at rls.py:300-302 and 331-333; with False, `not own_name_skipped` is True and the condition reduces to the prior `name if name in rules_by_table`, so matching is identical. Other RlsGuardRunner callers in the diff are tests. Counter-input considered: no rule-set file, an rls rule on `tables` with `information_schema.tables`; skip is False so the rule still applies (the diff's test_without_rule_sets_rls_still_matches_a_catalog_view_by_name covers this).

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:363-400 _catalog_filter: every view requires TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() (byte compare) and, for TABLES, TABLE_NAME in the listed tables; for COLUMNS and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE, (TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME) in the listed pairs. For KEY_COLUMN_USAGE a row also needs either all three REFERENCED_* fields NULL or REFERENCED_TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE() with the referenced (table, column) pair listed. I traced the hinted counterexamples. A referenced side in another database fails the schema check, so the row is dropped. A table that matches only case-insensitively fails the BINARY compare. That matches the existence check the code comment describes, so such a name cannot be a listed table. _catalog_body (403-421) projects only the fields in spec.kept, from the view definitions at 120-161, and aliases every other field to NULL. This leaves out row counts, sizes, defaults, comments and CONSTRAINT_NAME. A LIMIT keeps the derived table materialized. The doc text at docs/external/rule-sets.md:122 matches this behavior. The input I traced was a key row whose referenced side is in another database.

ci.yml:204-210 and 161-162 in the connectors-mysql84 job. (1) log_bin_trust_function_creators is still a valid dynamic global variable in MySQL 8.4 (deprecated, not removed). The 8.4 removals are mysql_native_password default, expire_logs_days and similar, not this variable, so SET GLOBAL as root works. (2) The user 'sqllens'@'%' is created by the image entrypoint through MYSQL_USER, so GRANT ALL ON sqllens_other.* to an existing user is valid. 8.4 no longer creates users implicitly via GRANT, but the user already exists. (3) The official mysql:8.4 image ships mysqladmin, and the docs and common health-check examples use it. The health command also uses -h 127.0.0.1 with a root password that matches MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD. This verification rests on my knowledge of MySQL 8.4 and the image, not on running the job, so a live CI run was not observed.

Traced rule_sets.py statically; I did not run the tests or sqlglot. _catalog_body (403-421) projects the TABLES fields (120-130) in order. Kept fields are TABLE_CATALOG, TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME and TABLE_TYPE, and every other field becomes NULL AS `X`. This matches _TABLES_FIELDS at test lines 312-319. The source is `information_schema`.`TABLES`. The filter for row_filter 'table' (375-381) is exp.and_(_in_schema('TABLE_SCHEMA'), In(CAST(`TABLE_NAME` AS BINARY), literals of the table names)). _in_schema (349-350) gives CAST(`TABLE_SCHEMA` AS BINARY) = CAST(CurrentSchema() AS BINARY). The test's own expectation at line 351 renders CurrentSchema as SCHEMA(). The LIMIT is _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = 18446744073709551615 (166, 420). All of this matches DERIVED_TABLES at test lines 320-325, with names 'customers', 'orders' consistent with the _PAIRS fixture. Exact whitespace and parenthesis rendering comes from sqlglot, which I could not execute. The test at 345-352 asserts equality against apply_rule_set output.

EXAMPLE_TABLES (tests/unit/_rule_set_fixtures.py:34) is {customers:(id,name), orders:(id,customer_id,total)}. _catalog_filter (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:382) builds pairs in that dict order, giving the _PAIRS order (customers,id),(customers,name),(orders,id),(orders,customer_id),(orders,total). The 'column' filter (line 383-385) is and_(CAST(TABLE_SCHEMA AS BINARY)=CAST(SCHEMA() AS BINARY), (CAST(TABLE_NAME),CAST(COLUMN_NAME)) IN pairs), which matches _COLUMNS_FILTER (test lines 330-333). The 'key' filter (388-400) is and_(own, paren(or_(no_reference, listed_reference))). The code builds own as an AND, which sqlglot's and_ wraps in parens when combined. no_reference is three IS NULL checks, and listed_reference is the schema check plus the pairs IN on REFERENCED_* fields. Both OR operands are parenthesized, and the whole OR is wrapped in a paren. This matches _KCU_FILTER (test lines 334-342). The paren placement relies on my recollection of sqlglot's and_/or_ wrapping and was not executed.

rule_sets.py:120 defines _CATALOG_VIEWS: dict[str, _CatalogView] with keys 'TABLES', 'COLUMNS', 'KEY_COLUMN_USAGE' (lines 121,131,147). _CatalogView (lines 93-114) is a frozen dataclass with fields: tuple[str, ...] (a sequence) and kept: frozenset[str] (a set). Counted _CATALOG_VIEWS in rule_sets.py:120-161. TABLES fields are 6+5+5+5 = 21 (lines 123-126). COLUMNS fields are 5+4+3+4+5+1 = 22 (lines 133-138). KEY_COLUMN_USAGE fields are 12 (lines 149-152). Kept counts are TABLES 4 (line 128), COLUMNS 12 (lines 140-144) and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE 9 (lines 154-158), which sum to 25. These match the MySQL 8.0 documented columns for the three views: TABLES has 21 (TABLE_CATALOG to TABLE_COMMENT), COLUMNS has 22 (through SRS_ID) and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE has 12. I took the MySQL column lists from memory and did not check them against a live server. The test at tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:392-400 asserts [21, 22, 12] and 25.

Traced apply_rls (src/sqllens/safety/rls.py) for 'SELECT orders.TABLE_NAME FROM information_schema.tables AS orders' with rule table 'orders'. First loop (298-311): name 'tables' is not in rules_by_table, so nothing is injected and the table id is not in injected_ids. It is a base source, so it is not added to reference_ids (316-320). Backstop loop (322-345): the name 'tables' does not match, so the alias 'orders' does. With skip_catalog_views=False, own_name_skipped is False and the name branch fails, so the alias branch matches. With skip_catalog_views=True, own_name_skipped is True, the name branch is disabled, and the alias branch still matches. In both cases the table is in neither injected_ids nor reference_ids, so RlsError('could not prove row-level-security scoping ...') is raised at 341-345. This matches the test at tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:734-745, which loops over skip in (False, True) with match='could not prove'.

rule_sets.py:319-327 _wrap (returned at line 316 for catalog views) uses the user's alias identifier copy if present (so `AS t` and bare `t` give `t`), else exp.to_identifier(table.name, quoted=True). table.name keeps the source letter case, so tables, TABLES and Tables give `tables`, `TABLES` and `Tables`, including for the backticked mixed-case reference. This matches the five parametrized cases in tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:355-369. I traced the code by reading and did not run the tests.

rule_sets.py:288-290: a catalog view with FORCE INDEX has 'hints' set, which is outside _TABLE_ARGS|{db}, so _check_wrappable (220-225) raises KIND_TABLE_OPTIONS because 'hints' is in _TABLE_OPTION_ARGS (171).
